$comment: CW Galaga's entries paced to the sound channel (#396), pinned for all three
ios/Sources/MorseKitCheck/main.swift and the android and desktop
GalagaPacingTest. Data, not code - see CLAUDE.md's separate-ports rule.
Every expected value below was worked out by hand from the rules in
'derivation', not captured from any port. Do not regenerate it to make a
failing test pass; change it only when a rule is meant to change.

derivation.problem: at its top waves CW Galaga enters an enemy every 0.5 s (0.375 s on Fast), faster than Morse at 15-20 WPM can announce them one at a time; announcements queued and up to a third of enemies dived and landed before their sound had played
derivation.channelFree: the sound channel is free at a time when nothing is sounding, the gap after the last sound has passed, and no arrival is waiting its turn. A waiting replay does not count: an arrival is announced ahead of it
derivation.rule: when the game paces its entries to the sound (hear-it mode), an entry that falls due while the channel is not free waits: the entry clock stops at the interval and the enemy is released on the first step the channel is free, at the start of its path (progress 0); the next entry falls due a full entryInterval after that release. A release makes the channel busy, so one step releases at most one paced entry. An entry released on time, on a free channel, is born partway along when the step overshot its due time, as before
derivation.unpaced: a game that does not pace (keying mode sounds nothing) ignores the channel and keeps the old schedule, releasing every entry a long step overshot
derivation.unchanged: flights, dives, the dive clock, the formation, timings and scoring are untouched: a held entry only waits
derivation.why it is fair: a paced entry's sound starts the step it enters, so a listener who answers 0.6 s after the sound ends shoots it at most longest-character + 0.6 s after entry (1.52 + 0.6 = 2.12 s for 0 at 15 WPM); the earliest it can land is entryTime + diveTime after entry (3.0 s on Normal, 2.25 s on Fast)
derivation.game: every scenario is wave 1 on Normal with a one-character pool [K]: entryInterval 1.4 s, entryTime 2.4 s, the first entry due 1.4 s in. 'entered' lists the Entered events of that step, in order, with the enemy's id and its progress along its entry path; 'released' is how many of the wave's formation have been released after the step

channel.$comment: Steps on one GameAnnouncer, in order. 'next' takes the sound the channel has at 'at' and starts it there, lasting durations[text] then 'gap'. 'check' does nothing. 'free' is isFree(at) after the step.

steps.note: an arrival waiting its turn holds it
K and its gap are over
a waiting replay does not hold an entry
a forgotten arrival no longer holds it
the replay E sounds 0.875 to 1.125, free at 1.5
a reset drops what waits and frees the channel

scenarios.name: on a free channel an entry comes on the interval, as before
a due entry waits while the channel is busy, then starts its path from the beginning

steps.note: the next is due a full interval after the held one's release

scenarios.name: a long step releases one paced entry; the next waits for the channel
a game that does not pace (keying) ignores the channel
